system_description.narrative_title: Gulf escalation: Iran, proxies, and attacks on shipping & allies
system_description.narrative_summary: A single dominant narrative is a widening Iran-led campaign and proxy violence that is extending conflict beyond traditional battlefields into critical maritime choke points (Strait of Hormuz, Bab el-Mandeb), neighbouring states (Bahrain, Saudi Arabia) and cyber/infra domains. The pattern combines mine and missile strikes on tankers, aerial and radar attacks on Gulf allies, Houthi advances in Yemen, and Iranian cyber tactics, while the US response oscillates between restraint and warnings—raising risks to global trade, energy flows, and regional stability. Regional alignments and missile proliferation further amplify systemic instability and feedbacks.
system_description.scope: State and proxy kinetic and cyber operations in the Gulf and Red Sea region; attacks on maritime traffic and port/early-warning infrastructure; regional military and naval deployments; diplomatic/political decisions by Iran, Gulf states, Turkey/Qatar, the US and allies; impacts on shipping, energy flows and regional security dynamics.
system_description.super_system: Global geopolitical order and international trade & energy security
adjacent_subsystems: Global energy markets (oil and LNG supply)
US domestic politics and foreign policy

variables.name: Maritime attack rate
variables.description: The frequency and intensity of kinetic and explosive attacks directed at commercial and non-combatant vessels in regional sea lanes.

variables.name: Coastal infrastructure damage
variables.description: The accumulated physical degradation and functionality loss of ports, radar/early‑warning sites, and shore-based maritime infrastructure.

variables.name: Naval deployment level
variables.description: The aggregate presence and disposition of surface and subsurface naval assets operating in and around critical chokepoints.

variables.name: Proxy force activity
variables.description: The rate and intensity of operations carried out by irregular or proxy armed groups in the maritime and littoral environment.

variables.name: Missile and drone strike rate
variables.description: The frequency of ballistic, cruise, and unmanned aerial launches directed at regional targets, including sea, land, and air targets.

variables.name: Missile capability growth
variables.description: The rate of acquisition, production, and deployment of missile and stand-off strike capabilities across regional actors and proxies.

variables.name: Cyber attack intensity
variables.description: The frequency and disruptive severity of offensive cyber operations targeting maritime, energy, or defence infrastructure.

variables.name: Shipping throughput
variables.description: The volume of commercial maritime traffic transiting through regional choke points and strategic sea lanes per unit time.

variables.name: Energy export flow
variables.description: The volumetric rate of hydrocarbon and LNG shipments leaving the region for international markets.

variables.name: Shipping and insurance cost level
variables.description: The prevailing premiums, risk surcharges, and operational costs borne by commercial shippers operating in the region.

variables.name: Regional political tension
variables.description: The aggregate degree of diplomatic strain, public hostility, and interstate friction among regional actors.

variables.name: Public support for military action
variables.description: The level of domestic public and political constituency backing for offensive or escalatory military measures.

variables.name: Engagement rules and constraints
variables.description: The set and strictness of operational, legal, and political constraints that govern the use of force by deployed forces.

variables.name: Coalition alignment cohesion
variables.description: The degree of policy, operational coordination, and shared objectives among external and regional partners.

variables.name: Early‑warning system integrity
variables.description: The operational reliability and coverage of radar, sensors, and information‑sharing systems used for threat detection.

variables.name: Maritime mine density
variables.description: The spatial concentration and operational status of naval mines and similar area-denial ordnance in key sea lanes.

catalysts.title: Continued mine attacks in Strait of Hormuz
catalysts.description: Repeated mine strikes and tanker damage in Hormuz are likely to continue, sustaining attacks on commercial shipping and area-denial hazards.
catalysts.rationale: Iran/IRGC report multiple tankers hit mines; three tankers on fire after mines in Hormuz (11-14 to 11-15 headlines).

catalysts.title: Houthis consolidate near Bab el‑Mandeb
catalysts.description: Houthis' territorial gains at the strait and missile launches increase proxy maritime threats and disrupt southern Red Sea transit.
catalysts.rationale: Yemeni government forces withdraw; Houthis in control of Bab el‑Mandeb and launched missiles (11-15, 11-16 headlines).

catalysts.title: Iran strikes Bahrain / claims US base attack
catalysts.description: Iranian attacks on Bahrain and claims of striking a US base raise risk of wider naval and aerial responses by regional partners and US forces.
catalysts.rationale: Multiple headlines: Iran attacks Bahrain, claims hit on US base; Bahrain issues alerts and intercepts (11-14 to 11-16).

catalysts.title: Sustained missile/drone strikes toward Saudi Arabia
catalysts.description: Ongoing ballistic and drone launches toward Saudi targets (Riyadh, Jazan) will likely continue, prompting air defenses and counterstrikes.
catalysts.rationale: Houthis say they launched ballistic missiles toward Riyadh; Saudi-led coalition intercepts missiles/drones (11-15 headlines).

catalysts.title: Expanded Iranian cyber operations affecting real-world systems
catalysts.description: Iran's evolving cyber playbook aims to create kinetic and infrastructural disruption, potentially degrading maritime sensors and operations.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'Iran’s New Cyber Playbook: Create Real-World Havoc' signals expanded cyber-to-kinetic operations (11-14).

catalysts.title: U.S. leadership signals delay in strikes
catalysts.description: U.S. signals (Trump) to hold off on strikes absent new provocations could restrain immediate kinetic responses and shape coalition behaviour.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: Trump may hold off on Iran attacks and reverses course, hails momentum toward ending Iran war (11-14).

catalysts.title: IAEA concern over enrichment prompts international response
catalysts.description: IAEA worries about Iranian enrichment could trigger sanctions, diplomatic moves, or military targeting that alter regional escalation dynamics.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: IAEA increasingly concerned about Iranian enrichment plant (11-14) — could prompt punitive or preventive measures.

catalysts.title: Turkey–Qatar mutual defence pact influences alignments
catalysts.description: New defence pact may shift regional diplomatic and military coordination, affecting coalition cohesion and response postures.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: Turkey, Qatar sign mutual defence agreement, pledge unified stance (11-14), altering regional alignments.
